notes: CONFORMS since kb/Work PB5419. Opposite a group the numeric operand is treated as moved to a group item of its own size in standard data format characters; a numeric literal has no stored image and its size is its digit count (IV.4.2.2.2.2 GR4), so ConditionRenderer.ComparisonText compares a literal as its digits whatever sign it was written with, the group image a MOVE of the literal to a group stores: G2 = -5 is true for '5 ' and false for '-5', with the literal on either side, in the statement and nested in an ELSE. A numeric ITEM keeps its own stored characters, sign included (kb/Work PB5106). retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/Emit/OperandText.cs#AsItemSizeTemporary (AsItemSizeTemporary became OperandText.AsItemCharacters, which INSPECT reads as well (kb/Work PB5375))

next.reason: 1985: "the numeric operand is treated as though it were moved to a group item of the same size as the numeric data item"; 2023: "For comparison, an alphanumeric group item shall be treated as an elementary alphanumeric data item.". 1985 compares the numeric as if group-moved, with no conversion and any sign kept. 2023 treats the group as elementary alphanumeric, so the elementary rule applies; the group-move case is gone.
